description: S458: the runtime check tests the BASE type before the predicate. take(n: number(>0)) is called with the number 7 (passes; @shown becomes 7) and then with the STRING "9" (refused: not a number — E-CONTRACT-001-RT, @shown keeps 7). Before S458 the check was `(n > 0)`, which JavaScript coerces: "9" > 0 is true, so a string inhabited `number(>0)`.
rationale: §53.3.4: "A `number(>0 && <10000)` value IS a `number`. The constrained type is a subtype of the base type" — a value that is not of the base type cannot inhabit the refinement; §53.4.5 the boundary check refuses it.
